summary: Raman alone cannot show that flake 2 is a monolayer. The data do show it is much thinner than flake 1 in terms of hBN signal, and that its E2g band sits +2.8 ± 0.25 cm⁻¹ above flake 1's. That upshift is in the range Gorbachev et al. (2011) associate with a monolayer, but substrate strain and sample-to-sample scatter produce similar shifts, so it is not a clean monolayer marker. My reading: flake 2 is a thin hBN flake, plausibly 1 to a few layers; a monolayer is possible but unconfirmed. The decisive measurements are AFM thickness of both flakes and the low-frequency shear mode (10 to 100 cm⁻¹), which these spectra (starting at 450 cm⁻¹) do not cover.

observations.finding: Flake 1 shows the hBN E2g band at 1366.20 cm⁻¹, bulk-like, with a Lorentzian FWHM of 17.99 cm⁻¹ (height ≈3230 counts above the sloping background). The Si first-order line is at 520.90 cm⁻¹.
observations.evidence: Lorentzian + linear baseline fit, window 1320–1415 cm⁻¹ (E2g): centre 1366.20 ± 0.04, FWHM 17.99 ± 0.16, area 91,385 ± 755 (counts·cm⁻¹). Si window 505–537: centre 520.90 ± 0.05, FWHM 3.32 ± 0.18, area 5,102 ± 232. Residual rms 41 counts vs point-noise ≈38 counts. Centre unchanged (1366.19–1366.20) across windows 1300–1440 and 1340–1400 and with quadratic baselines.

observations.finding: Flake 2 shows a weak hBN E2g band at 1368.96 cm⁻¹, about 2.8 cm⁻¹ above flake 1. The band is real but small (height ≈270 counts above a ≈1600-count baseline).
observations.evidence: Same fit model: centre 1368.96 ± 0.25 (statistical), FWHM 22.2 ± 1.0, area 9,404 ± 444, height 270 counts. Point-to-point noise on the flat region is 17.9 counts, so the height SNR is about 15. Centre stays between 1368.96 and 1369.17 across the three windows and linear/quadratic baselines. Si line at 520.90 ± 0.00, area 98,955, height ≈18,000 counts.

observations.finding: Differential E2g shift of flake 2 relative to flake 1 is +2.76 ± 0.25 cm⁻¹. Both spectra have the same Si position (520.90), so this difference does not depend on the Si calibration offset.
observations.evidence: 1368.96 − 1366.20 = 2.76, uncertainty from quadrature of the two centre errors (0.25 and 0.04). Absolute upshift relative to the ~1366 cm⁻¹ bulk value is about +2.6 to +2.8 cm⁻¹, depending on whether the Si reference is 520.7 (assumed standard value, not verified from a cited source here) or 520.9.
observations.source: Bulk E2g ≈1366 cm⁻¹ as stated in Gorbachev et al., arXiv:1008.2868, text for Fig. 4 (their bulk hBN crystals)

observations.finding: Relative to the Si substrate, the hBN E2g signal is about 190× weaker in flake 2 than in flake 1. In absolute terms, the flake 2 E2g area is about 10% of flake 1's, while the Si area is about 19× larger in flake 2.
observations.evidence: hBN/Si integrated-area ratio: flake 1 = 17.9 ± 0.8, flake 2 = 0.095 ± 0.004; flake2/flake1 = 0.0053 (1/188). Absolute hBN area flake2/flake1 = 0.103. Si area flake2/flake1 = 19.4. The Si difference shows the optical stack differs strongly between the two spots (interference and/or coverage), so the ratio is not a clean thickness measure.

observations.finding: The 1369 cm⁻¹ feature in flake 2 is unlikely to be amorphous carbon contamination, because there is no G-like band near 1580 cm⁻¹ above noise.
observations.evidence: Flake 2 baseline over 1500–1650 cm⁻¹ is flat within noise (std 17.8 counts, point noise 17.9) with no structure at ~1580. Weak argument: contamination could be sparse.

observations.finding: Flake 2 has a broad bump near 950–980 cm⁻¹ (height ≈560 counts above baseline). This lies in the Si second-order region and is not reliably fitted. Flake 1 has a strongly sloping background from ~500 counts at 450 cm⁻¹ to ~1100 at 1650 cm⁻¹.
observations.evidence: Flake 2 bump: maximum 2188 counts at 951.9 cm⁻¹ over ~1600 background; the second-order fit did not converge (no stderr). Flake 1 background: ~400–500 counts at 450–500 cm⁻¹ rising to ~1000 at 1100 and ~1100–1200 at 1600–1650.

properties.name: layers
properties.value: not determined; flake 2 is thinner than flake 1 by hBN signal, and monolayer is possible but not established (1 to few layers)
properties.source: Gorbachev et al., arXiv:1008.2868 (abstract: monolayer upshift up to 4 cm⁻¹; integer-step intensity change with layer number); Cai et al., doi:10.1039/c6nr09312d and Ontaneda et al., doi:10.1088/1361-648X/aab883 (intrinsic monolayer shift debated)

properties.name: strain_sign
properties.value: undetermined; the +2.8 cm⁻¹ upshift is consistent with compressive strain (blue shift) but also with substrate-induced shifts and sample variation
properties.source: Okonai et al., doi:10.1039/d5na00283d (compressive strain blue-shifts E2g in CVD hBN); Cai et al., doi:10.1039/c6nr09312d (substrate-induced strain shifts E2g)

properties.name: phase
properties.value: hexagonal BN, layered; E2g at 1366 cm⁻¹ in flake 1
properties.source: Gorbachev et al., arXiv:1008.2868, Fig. 4 text (E2g ≈1366 cm⁻¹ for bulk hBN)

properties.name: defect_level
properties.value: not determined; FWHM (18 cm⁻¹ in flake 1, 22 cm⁻¹ in flake 2) cannot be interpreted without the instrument resolution and a reference width

caveats: Spot coverage: the flake 2 Si signal is about 19× stronger than flake 1's, so the laser spot may be mostly on bare SiO2/Si. A smaller hBN coverage within the spot would cut the E2g intensity without implying a monolayer. Peak position is less affected by coverage than intensity is.

Intensity is not calibrated: no bare SiO2/Si reference was supplied, and the optical interference of the 290 nm SiO2 stack changes Si and hBN signals differently. The 190× drop in hBN/Si cannot be converted to a layer count here.
Si calibration: the 520.7 cm⁻¹ reference is an assumed standard value, not taken from a cited source in this session. The differential shift (+2.76 cm⁻¹) does not depend on it.

Detector saturation: the two top Si points in flake 2 are 18,777.5 and 18,764.8 counts, with a symmetric profile. Saturation cannot be excluded without the detector's full-well level; if it saturates, the Si area is underestimated and the hBN/Si ratio shifts.
Fit statistics: flake 2 E2g centre ±0.25 cm⁻¹ is statistical only. The peak has height SNR ≈15, and its width (22 cm⁻¹) is poorly constrained by a ~300-count bump on a sloping background.

Reduced χ² was not used (no per-point σ supplied); fit quality is judged from residual rms against point-to-point noise. The lmfit Lorentzian amplitude is the integrated area, so areas are A (earlier intermediate values using πAσ were wrong and have been replaced).

Literature use: I used the abstracts and captions of Gorbachev et al. (Small 2011), Cai et al., Ontaneda et al., Krečmarová et al., Stenger et al., and Okonai et al.; I did not view the figure images, so the stepwise intensity law and the ±2 cm⁻¹ sample scatter are taken from the Fig. 4 caption and abstract text only.

Skill scripts and reference notes live outside this project folder, and I was asked not to read files outside it. I did not use the skill's reference notes or scripts; the analysis is my own, from the two CSV files.
questions_for_user: AFM height (or step count) of flake 2 and flake 1. This is the most decisive check: it calibrates the intensity and upshift against actual thickness and tells us whether flake 2 is a monolayer.

Did you record the low-frequency region (about 10–100 cm⁻¹)? The interlayer shear mode of hBN (52.5 cm⁻¹ in bulk, down to 46.0 cm⁻¹ in 3 layers, discrete below 8 layers) is a direct layer-number fingerprint (Stenger et al., arXiv:1705.01298). A notch-filter scan of that region would settle the layer count far better than E2g intensity.

Is flake 2 fully covering the laser spot? An optical image with the spot overlaid, or the flake's lateral size compared with the spot size, would show whether the low hBN intensity comes from thickness or from partial coverage.
Do you have a bare SiO2/Si reference spectrum under identical conditions? It would give the Si intensity without hBN, which is needed to normalise intensities between flakes.

Detector saturation level and the laser power at the sample / spot size / objective NA. The flake 2 Si peak is about 18,000 counts, and the top points are nearly equal, so saturation must be excluded.

Spectrometer resolution (grating and slit), and whether any background or fluorescence subtraction was applied. Flake 1 has a strong sloping background, and the Si FWHM of 3.3–3.5 cm⁻¹ suggests the instrumental width is comparable to the spectral features.
Were the two flakes measured on the same day with the same focus and substrate position? Focus and interference can shift the Si and hBN intensities independently of thickness.
The 1368.96 cm⁻¹ band in flake 2 and the 950–980 cm⁻¹ bump: are they reproducible at other spots on flake 2? A single spectrum per flake is not enough to assign a monolayer.
citations: [arXiv:1008.2868](https://arxiv.org/abs/1008.2868) — Gorbachev et al., Small (2011), doi:10.1002/smll.201001628. Abstract: monolayer upshift of the fundamental Raman mode by up to 4 cm⁻¹; integer-step Raman intensity change with layer number. Fig. 4 caption: monolayer/bilayer position varies by ±2 cm⁻¹ between samples; integrated intensity IT vs N (left inset). Text of Fig. 3: optical contrast of a monolayer on SiO2 is expected to be maximal at 80 ± 10 nm SiO2 thickness.

[doi:10.1039/c6nr09312d](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28191567/) — Cai et al., Nanoscale (2017). Abstract: intrinsic E2g of BN does not depend sensibly on layer number; substrate-induced strain can cause a pronounced Raman shift.

[doi:10.1088/1361-648X/aab883](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.08454) — Ontaneda et al., J. Phys.: Condens. Matter (2018). Abstract: intrinsic monolayer shift is small; thermal expansion makes it nearly vanish at room temperature (DFT), which may explain small observed shifts in suspended samples.

[doi:10.3390/nano9071047](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31336572/) — Krečmarová et al., Nanomaterials 9, 1047 (2019). Abstract: E2g shows only weak thickness dependence on SiO2/Si; substrate can reduce the shift; optical contrast is the most suitable fast thickness method for few-layer hBN on SiO2/Si.

[arXiv:1705.01298](https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.01298) — Stenger et al. (2017). Abstract: interlayer shear mode at 52.5 cm⁻¹ in bulk hBN, 46.0(5) cm⁻¹ for 3 layers; discrete values below ~4 nm; quantitative layer count below 8 layers.

[doi:10.1039/d5na00283d](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40959728/) — Okonai et al., Nanoscale Advances (2025). Abstract: compressive strain blue-shifts the E2g band (to 1415 cm⁻¹ at grain centres in CVD multilayer hBN; strain −1.23%).
limits: Layer number is not determined. The two spectra alone cannot give it: there is no calibrated monolayer reference, no bare-substrate reference, and no AFM thickness.

The +2.8 cm⁻¹ upshift is not an unambiguous monolayer marker at room temperature on SiO2. Gorbachev (2011) reports up to 4 cm⁻¹ with ±2 cm⁻¹ sample scatter; Cai (2017) and Ontaneda (2018) argue the intrinsic shift is small or absent; substrate strain shifts E2g.

Intensity-based thickness (hBN/Si, E2g area) needs a calibration I do not have. Under a naive linear law (I ∝ N), flake 2 would be ~0.10 × N1, where N1 is flake 1's layer number, so flake 2 is monolayer only if flake 1 has about 10 layers or fewer. N1 is unknown, and the linear law is assumed, not measured. Interference in the SiO2 stack makes Si and hBN intensities non-linear in thickness.
The 1366 cm⁻¹ and 1369 cm⁻¹ E2g positions are fit-statistics values. Calibration uncertainty (Si reference offset) is a few tenths of a cm⁻¹ and does not change the differential shift.
Rejected: amorphous carbon contamination as the origin of the 1369 cm⁻¹ band in flake 2 (no G band near 1580 cm⁻¹). Not fully excluded, since contamination can be sparse.

Relations not applied: the shear-mode layer relation (Stenger et al.) and the optical-contrast thickness relation (Krečmarová et al.; Gorbachev et al.) need data outside this folder (low-frequency spectrum; optical contrast on a calibrated microscope).

I did not use the raman-analysis skill's reference notes or scripts, which live outside this project folder. Mode assignment is limited to hBN E2g, and Si lines are labelled 'Si substrate'. I did not check the matcher's library, since the folder was not used for that.
Only one spectrum per flake, with no replicates or spot-to-spot statistics. Flake-to-flake differences could reflect spot placement or coverage.
